summary: Carefully executed, provenance-traced paired preregistered study of a verifier‑grounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline for intent→configuration NetOps tasks in a Mininet emulation (N=200 pairs, shared_initial_candidate). Analysis followed the preregistered McNemar paired test (exact p=0.125) as primary inferential result; archived paired bootstrap CI [0.005,0.04] is presented as an auxiliary estimator and is appropriately discussed. Artifacts, verifier traces, and provenance (including master_prompt reference) are archived. No unreported deviations or missingness were found. Study is careful and reproducible, but a few manuscript-level corrections are required before finalisation.
required_revisions: Provide a conventional IEEE numbered References section with full bibliographic metadata (authors, title, venue, year, DOI/arXiv) for every cited record; remove or replace any bare DOI/arXiv/identifier‑only entries in the manuscript body and References. This must be resolvable from the archived cited_record_ids and verification artifacts.

Make the bootstrap CI role and interpretation unequivocally secondary in the Abstract and Conclusions: explicitly label the paired bootstrap CI as descriptive/exploratory, and avoid wording that could be read as implying confirmatory evidence when the preregistered McNemar test did not reject (p=0.125). A concise sentence in Abstract and one in Results/Conclusion suffices.

Condense the Disclosure Statement to a concise paragraph within the five pages that preserves the mandatory master_prompt path+SHA‑256 and the key provenance facts required by the track, removing verbatim execution logs or duplicated numeric accounting already reported in Methods/Results (artifact hashes and full manifests may remain only in the archived bundle).

In Methods or Results, add a single clarifying sentence that points readers to the archived analysis code and exact test implementation (artifact path and hash are already present) and state that McNemar exact two‑sided test was the preregistered primary inferential procedure (the manuscript already records this but must explicitly link to the archived analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis_log.jsonl for reproducibility).
optional_revisions: Consider adding one short paragraph in Threats to Validity quantifying the low baseline failure prevalence effect on power (illustrate how observed baseline 98% success compares to preregistered power assumptions) to help readers interpret the non‑significant primary test together with the bootstrap CI.
If space permits, include the 2×2 contingency table (n11/n10/n01/n00) as a small inline table or figure caption to aid quick verification (these counts are in archived artifacts).

Spell out in one sentence why provider model temperature = null/unset is recorded and how readers should interpret that value (the manuscript already states null/unset does not imply temperature=0; a one‑line restatement in Methods improves clarity).
